name: Seir
title: Horite and ancestor of the land of Seir
summary: Seir was a Horite patriarch who gave his name to the mountainous region of Seir in the Edom area southeast of the Dead Sea. The area was later taken over by Esau's descendants, the Edomites. Seir is mentioned in the Bible primarily as a geographical and genealogical reference linked to the original Horite population in this mountainous region.

keyEvents.title: The Sons of Seir and the Genealogy of the Horites
keyEvents.description: The sons of Seir are mentioned as the chiefs of the Horites who lived in the land, and their family lines are listed in detail.

keyEvents.title: The Original Settlement of the Horites in the Mountains of Seir
keyEvents.description: The Horites, descendants of Seir, were the original inhabitants of the mountain region that took his name, before they were driven out by the Edomites.

keyEvents.title: Esau's Settlement in the Land of Seir
keyEvents.description: Esau settled in the mountains of Seir, and his descendants gradually took over the area from the Horites, the original people of Seir.

keyEvents.title: The Chiefs of Seir
keyEvents.description: Seir's descendants organized themselves as chiefs in the land of the Horites, showing their political significance in the region.

keyEvents.title: The Mountains of Seir in Israel's History
keyEvents.description: The mountains of Seir, which bear his name, play an important role in the journey of the Israelites, since God gave this land to Esau's descendants and forbade Israel from taking it.
